SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: Taurus's book for the 92 is short: a six-step field strip on two pages, a magazine strip, and a line telling the owner to stop there. Every step below carries the book's own words and the printed page they sit on; where the book is silent, the guide says so rather than filling the gap.

steps.title: Confirm the pistol is the 92 this book describes
steps.action: Check the gun against the book's specifications table before you start: a 9mm Luger DA/SA pistol with a 5-inch barrel, 17+1 capacity and an ambidextrous manual safety / decocker. The book describes that one configuration and no other.
steps.prose: Taurus warns in the same book that firearms which look alike differ in their controls, and this book is a supplement that names only the 92. If your pistol's barrel length, capacity or safety arrangement does not match the table, this procedure is not confirmed for it - find the book for your model on TaurusUSA.com before taking anything apart.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Specifications, printed pp.14-15 (PDF p.8)

steps.title: Magazine out, slide locked back, then look and feel
steps.action: Finger off the trigger and the muzzle in a safe direction, press the magazine release button and remove the magazine. Pull the slide to the rear and lock it back, then look into the magazine well and the chamber and put a finger into both.
steps.prose: The order is the point: magazine first, then the slide. Racking a slide with a loaded magazine still seated only feeds the next round into the chamber. The finger check is part of Taurus's own instruction, not an extra - a case head deep in a 9mm chamber is easy to miss by eye under bench light.
steps.quote: 1. Before disassembly always (1) Keep your finger off or the trigger, (2) point the muzzle in a safe direction (3) remove the magazine by pressing the magazine release button (4) pulling the slide to the rear and locking back and (5) looking and feeling the magazine well and chamber to confirm the pistol is empty. An empty firearm cannot fire.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.26-27 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: After removing the magazine, always check the chamber and make sure it is empty.

steps.title: No magazine disconnect - an empty well is not an empty gun
steps.action: Treat the pistol as loaded until you have seen and felt an empty chamber, even with the magazine already on the bench. Taurus states plainly that the 92 fires the chambered round with no magazine in it.
steps.prose: Dropping the magazine changes nothing about a round already in the chamber. That is why the chamber check in the previous step is the step that makes the pistol safe to work on, and why it is done every time, not only when you think the gun was loaded.
steps.caution: Taurus's book also says the manual safety must be all the way in the safe position to work - never halfway. A safety lever is not a substitute for an empty chamber.
steps.quote: The Taurus® 92 does not have a magazine disconnect (magazine safety). They will fire the round in the chamber with the magazine removed.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Operating Instructions, printed pp.22-23 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Press the latch release and turn the disassembling latch
steps.action: Press the disassembling latch release and, while holding it in, rotate the disassembling latch 90 degrees clockwise. The book's parts illustration labels both controls on the frame.
steps.prose: Taurus warns on the same page that the slide can be scratched while the latch is being worked, so turn the latch with control rather than levering it with a tool against the slide. The book does not say whether the slide is let forward from the locked-back position before this step; it simply follows the empty-check with the latch.
steps.quote: 2. Press the disassembling latch release and rotate the disassembling latch 90 degrees clockwise.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.26-27 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: While removing the disassembly latch, make sure that the slide won’t be damaged (scratched).

steps.title: Pull the slide and barrel forward off the frame
steps.action: Pull the slide-barrel assembly forward and off the frame as one unit. The recoil spring and its guide come with it, under compression.
steps.prose: The recoil spring is loaded against its guide rod inside the slide, and Taurus warns about it launching out. Keep the slide-barrel assembly under control in your hand as it clears the frame rails rather than letting it drop free.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.26-27 (PDF p.14)
steps.warn: Take care to prevent the forcible ejection of the guide rod assembly and compressed recoil spring.

steps.title: Lift the recoil spring assembly off the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down. Release the recoil spring assembly from its seat on the bottom of the barrel, then lift it out carefully.
steps.prose: Taurus says to do this carefully for a reason: the spring is still compressed until the assembly is clear of its seat. Keep a thumb over it as it comes free so it cannot spring out of the slide.
steps.quote: 4. Release recoil spring assembly from its position on the bottom of the barrel. Lift and remove it carefully.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.28-29 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Press the locking block plunger forward
steps.action: With the spring assembly out, press the locking block plunger forward. This frees the barrel's locking block so the barrel can come out of the slide.
steps.prose: The locking block and its plunger are part of the barrel assembly in Taurus's parts list. Pressing the plunger is the only thing the book asks of them - neither part is removed from the barrel.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.28-29 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Barrel out - forward, then up
steps.action: Holding the plunger forward, remove the barrel from the slide by pulling it to the front and up. Forward first, up second.
steps.prose: With the barrel in your hand, look down the bore against a light before cleaning it. Taurus's own instruction after an odd-sounding shot is exactly this check: if you do not see light, something is stuck in the bore, and the pistol is not fired again until a qualified gunsmith or Taurus has dealt with it.
steps.aside: Once the barrel is removed from the slide, look down the bore. If you do not see light, there is something stuck in the bore.
steps.quote: 6. Remove the barrel from the slide by pulling to the front and up.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.28-29 (PDF p.15)

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel and recoil spring assembly: that is the whole of the 92's field strip. Taurus stops the owner here - the firing pin, firing pin block, extractor, hammer, sear and trigger parts stay where they are.
steps.prose: The exploded view at the back of the book lists more than fifty parts, but it is a parts list, not a procedure. The one further thing the book does publish is the magazine strip, which is where Deep Clean goes. Taurus says the pistol may be cleaned and lubricated under normal conditions with the field strip alone.
steps.quote: No further cleaning or disassembly is recommended unless done by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembly, printed pp.28-29 (PDF p.15)

deepSteps.title: Punch the magazine plate, pull the bottom out
deepSteps.action: Use a punch to press the magazine plate down, then pull the magazine bottom out of the magazine body. Keep a thumb over the opening as the bottom comes free.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is compressed under the plate, and Taurus warns that both can be ejected forcibly. Wear eye protection for this; Taurus's disassembly section asks for ANSI Z87.1+ eyewear every time the pistol is handled for cleaning and maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: 1. Use a punch to press the magazine plate down, then pull the magazine bottom out of the magazine body.
deepSteps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembling Your Magazine, printed pp.30-31 (PDF p.16)
deepSteps.warn: Please take care to prevent the forcible ejection of the magazine spring plate and compressed magazine spring.

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower out
deepSteps.action: Withdraw the magazine spring plate and the magazine spring from the body. Turn the body upside down and the follower comes out.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way the spring and follower sat before they leave the body, so they go back in the same way. Clean the inside of the body and the follower and remove the excess oil - Taurus's care section asks for a light film and no more.
deepSteps.quote: 2. Withdraw the magazine spring plate and magazine spring from the magazine body. Turn the magazine upside down and remove the magazine follower.
deepSteps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembling Your Magazine, printed pp.30-31 (PDF p.16)

deepSteps.title: Reassemble the magazine in reverse order
deepSteps.action: Follower in first, then the spring and spring plate, then slide the magazine bottom back onto the body until the plate holds it. That is the reverse of the strip.
deepSteps.prose: This is the end of what Taurus publishes for the owner. Nothing beyond the field strip and the magazine is part of a 92 clean; the book sends anything further to a qualified gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite:
92
SUPPLEMENT INSTRUCTION MANUAL — REV. 4 — Disassembling Your Magazine, printed pp.30-31 (PDF p.16)

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Clean the bore and leave it free of debris
Run a lightly oiled cloth or patch through the bore, the same way as the outside of the pistol, then remove the excess oil
Look down the bore with the barrel out of the slide: no light means something is stuck in it
Never fire the pistol with an obstruction in the bore - take it to a qualified gunsmith or contact Taurus

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & RECOIL SPRING
tasks: Remove dust from all crevices with a small clean brush
Rub the slide, frame and recoil spring assembly with a lightly oiled cloth
Leave a light film of good quality gun oil to prevent corrosion, and remove the excess
Do not clean a pistol fitted with a laser in a well or ultrasonic machine that submerges it - it can damage the laser

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the magazine body clean with a lightly oiled cloth and remove the excess oil
Check that the feed lips and follower are free of dust and grit
The magazine strip is in Deep Clean

reassembly: Taurus's whole instruction is to reverse the disassembly steps, so work back through them in order.
Press the locking block plunger forward and put the barrel back into the slide, back and down - the reverse of front and up.
Seat the recoil spring assembly back in its position on the bottom of the barrel, under control - the spring is compressed as it goes in.
Run the slide-barrel assembly back onto the frame from the front.
Press the disassembling latch release and rotate the disassembling latch back 90 degrees, counterclockwise, to its closed position, taking care not to scratch the slide.
Check that the manual safety lever moves fully up (on) and fully down; Taurus warns that a lever not completely in the off position will damage the pistol.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty and no magazine in it: the slide should run its full stroke and return fully forward under the recoil spring; pulled fully to the rear, the slide should lock back on the slide catch the way the empty-check locks it, and pressing the slide catch should send it forward. The manual safety lever must go all the way up to safe and all the way down - moving it down decocks the hammer - and never rest halfway. Taurus's book publishes no further function test; if anything does not work as described, the pistol goes to a qualified gunsmith or Taurus Customer Care before it is fired.
